headword: {国民|こくみん}の{祝日|しゅくじつ}
reading: こくみんのしゅくじつ

definitions.explanation: An officially designated public holiday in Japan. Defined by the National Holiday Law (国民の祝日に関する法律). Japan currently has 16 national holidays throughout the year.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}は{国民|こくみん}の{祝日|しゅくじつ}で{休|やす}みだ。
examples.english: Tomorrow is a national holiday so we have the day off.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}には{年間|ねんかん}16の{国民|こくみん}の{祝日|しゅくじつ}がある。
examples.english: Japan has 16 national holidays per year.

examples.japanese: {国民|こくみん}の{祝日|しゅくじつ}が{月曜日|げつようび}になる「ハッピーマンデー{制度|せいど}」で{連休|れんきゅう}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: The 'Happy Monday' system, which moves national holidays to Mondays, has increased the number of long weekends.

notes:
The official term for Japan's legally designated public holidays, as defined by the {国民|こくみん}の{祝日|しゅくじつ}に{関|かん}する{法律|ほうりつ} (Act on National Holidays). In everyday speech, people often just say {祝日|しゅくじつ}.

JAPAN'S 16 NATIONAL HOLIDAYS:
- {元日|がんじつ} (Jan 1): New Year's Day
- {成人|せいじん}の{日|ひ} (2nd Mon Jan): Coming of Age Day
- {建国記念|けんこくきねん}の{日|ひ} (Feb 11): National Foundation Day
- {天皇誕生日|てんのうたんじょうび} (Feb 23): Emperor's Birthday
- {春分|しゅんぶん}の{日|ひ} (Mar ~21): Vernal Equinox Day
- {昭和|しょうわ}の{日|ひ} (Apr 29): Showa Day
- {憲法記念日|けんぽうきねんび} (May 3): Constitution Memorial Day
- みどりの{日|ひ} (May 4): Greenery Day
- こどもの{日|ひ} (May 5): Children's Day
- {海|うみ}の{日|ひ} (3rd Mon Jul): Marine Day
- {山|やま}の{日|ひ} (Aug 11): Mountain Day
- {敬老|けいろう}の{日|ひ} (3rd Mon Sep): Respect for the Aged Day
- {秋分|しゅうぶん}の{日|ひ} (Sep ~23): Autumnal Equinox Day
- スポーツの{日|ひ} (2nd Mon Oct): Sports Day
- {文化|ぶんか}の{日|ひ} (Nov 3): Culture Day
- {勤労感謝|きんろうかんしゃ}の{日|ひ} (Nov 23): Labor Thanksgiving Day

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {祝日|しゅくじつ}: holiday — the common short form used in everyday speech
- {祭日|さいじつ}: festival day — an older term sometimes used interchangeably with {祝日|しゅくじつ}, though strictly they differ
- {休日|きゅうじつ}: day off — broader term for any non-working day, including weekends
